sources.entry: Claude Code GitHub Action by Anthropic - The official GitHub Action for running Claude Code in CI: mention @claude in issues and pull requests to delegate code changes, reviews, and fixes.

summary.one_liner: A GitHub Action that runs Claude Code on your own runner so you can mention @claude in issues and pull requests to get questions answered, code reviews, and code changes.
summary.what_it_does: The action runs Claude Code inside a GitHub Actions workflow and activates based on context: responding to @claude mentions, issue assignments, or explicit automation prompts. It can answer questions about code, review PR changes and suggest improvements, and implement fixes, refactors, or new features, with results posted as GitHub comments and PR reviews. It shows progress checkboxes that update as tasks complete. Structured JSON outputs can be exposed as GitHub Action outputs for downstream automation. Authentication is supported through the Anthropic direct API (API key or workload identity federation), Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Microsoft Foundry. Additional tools and MCP servers can be enabled through configuration.
use_cases: delegate code changes from a GitHub issue or PR comment
answer questions about a codebase in PR threads
how_to_run: Open claude in the terminal and run /install-github-app (direct Anthropic API users; requires repository admin rights)
For AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, or Microsoft Foundry, see docs/cloud-providers.md
Add a workflow file that uses the action and configure the prompt and claude_args inputs (see Usage Guide)
notable: Automatically detects execution mode from workflow context, with no mode configuration needed
Runs entirely on the user's own GitHub runner; only model API calls go to the chosen provider
Unified prompt and claude_args inputs aligned with the Claude Code SDK
Structured JSON outputs become GitHub Action outputs
Documented solutions guide with ready-made workflow patterns such as path-specific and external-contributor reviews
caveats: Quickstart via /install-github-app is only available for direct Anthropic API users; other providers need manual setup
Installing the GitHub app and adding secrets requires repository admin rights
Upgrading from v0.x requires following the migration guide, as configuration changed in v1.0
